title: Networks: addresses and ports
summary: IP addresses, names, ports, and what listening on 0.0.0.0 means.

text: Machines talk with numbers, IP addresses. DNS turns names into addresses.
- 203.0.113.10 is an address kept for examples; dig shows the real one.
One machine runs many services. The port says which one you want.
- A service listens on its port; a client connects to it.
- 127.0.0.1 (localhost) is the machine itself: no other machine can connect.
- 0.0.0.0 means every address the machine has: open to the network.
- A database on 0.0.0.0 by mistake is a classic security hole.
- ss -tln: t = TCP, l = listening, n = numbers instead of names.
